_readme: Buckets starting with _ are notes and are skipped by the script.
Entries are either a feed URL string, or {"sitemap":..., "match":...}.
IMPORTANT: run report-all, not report. Buckets roll up into verticals
(see VERTICAL_OF in topicwatch.py) and each vertical gets its own report.
Pooling five unrelated vocabularies into one ranking destroys the signal.
VERIFICATION STATUS: these are the standard published feed paths for these
outlets. I verified a handful directly; the rest are unconfirmed. Expect
some failures on the first run - the log now names each dead feed. Run
python topicwatch.py discover <domain> on any you want to rescue,
and delete the ones you do not.
_read_this_first: You now have several verticals. That is a lot of reading and most of it
will not change what you publish. Ranked by likely value to you:
1. boutique    - the shops you actually compete with. STILL EMPTY.
Worth more than everything else in this file combined.
2. seo_press   - where the AI-SEO vocabulary gets coined.
3. smb_growth  - your buyer's own vocabulary, in their words.
4. trade_press - what your agency competitors echo about 3 weeks later.
5. ai_business - applied AI, close to how buyers talk.
6. ai_press    - mostly model releases and funding. Low signal for you.
fintech and devtools are here because you asked. Be honest about whether
those are your buyers' industries or just adjacent interests. If you are
not selling into them specifically, they are noise you pay for in reading
time. Deleting a bucket is one line.
_ai_note: Two flavours of AI coverage. ai_press is product and research news;
ai_business is the applied and enterprise angle. The second is far more
useful to you - it is closer to how your buyer talks about AI.
